questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which of the following animals is capable of photosynthesis?
A. Sea slug
B. Jellyfish
C. Starfish
Answer: A. The sea slug, specifically the Elysia chlorotica, can acquire this ability temporarily by incorporating chloroplasts from the algae it consumes into its own cells, allowing it to convert sunlight into energy.
questions.de: Welche Art von Tier, etwa Elysia chlorotica, kann Photosynthese betreiben, indem es die Chloroplasten der gefressenen Algen in seine eigenen Zellen einbaut?
questions.en: What kind of animal, such as Elysia chlorotica, can photosynthesize by taking the chloroplasts of the algae it eats into its own cells?

timeline.labelEn: Augustus Addison Gould describes the sea slug Elysia chlorotica
timeline.labelDe: Augustus Addison Gould beschreibt die Meeresschnecke Elysia chlorotica

questions.notes: Wikipedia: Elysia chlorotica (a sacoglossan sea slug) keeps algal chloroplasts (kleptoplasty) that keep photosynthesizing for up to 9–10 months; however, later studies found such slugs survive just as well in the dark, so how much energy photosynthesis actually supplies is disputed.

questions.cardText:
[Medical Sciences] What is the neurological condition Synesthesia?
A. It involves the merging of sensory experiences, like “seeing” sounds
B. It leads to a temporary loss of one or more senses
C. It is the enhanced memory recall of two related sensory stimuli
Answer: A.
questions.de: Wie heißt das Phänomen, bei dem die Reizung eines Sinnes unwillkürlich Wahrnehmungen in einem anderen auslöst, etwa das „Sehen“ von Tönen?
questions.en: What is the name of the phenomenon in which stimulating one sense involuntarily triggers experiences in another, such as "seeing" sounds?

timeline.labelEn: Georg Tobias Ludwig Sachs publishes the first documented case of synesthesia
timeline.labelDe: Georg Tobias Ludwig Sachs veröffentlicht den ersten dokumentierten Fall von Synästhesie

questions.notes: Wikipedia calls synesthesia a perceptual phenomenon rather than a condition/disorder.
